antisense oligodeoxynucleotide (oligodeoxyribonucelotide) (oligo[dN])s specific to the initiation sites of S-, pre C- and P- genes of HBV inhibited the replication of HBV in HepG2 cell lines transfected with a HBV DNA.

antisense oligodeoxynucleotides directed at the translational initiation site of S, preC and P genes of hepatitis B virus inhibit hepatitis B surface antigen expression and hepatitis B viral DNA replication in HepG-2 cells harboring an HBV genome.
antisense oligodeoxynucleotides directed at translational sites of HBV genome inhibited the replication of HBV in HepG2 cell line transfected with a HBV genome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the inhibition of HBV replication in HepG 2 cells harboring HBV DNA by the treatment of antisense oligodesoxyribonucleotide(oligo [dN])s directed at the translational initiation site of HBV genes.
the inhibition of HBV replication in HepG 2 cells by antisense oligo(dNs) specific to the translating initiation sites of the S, pre C or P genes of HBsAg, and the effect on cell growth.
the inhibition of HBV replication in HepG1 cells by antisense oligo[deoxyribonucleotide]s.

antisense oligodeoxynucleotides directed at the translational initiation site of S, preC, or P genes of HBsAg are capable of suppressing HBV propagation.
the use of antisense oligonucleotides is a promising strategy for the treatment of chronic HBV infection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antisense oligo(dNs) directed to the translational start sites of the S, PreC, and P genes in HBV genome were synthesized and used for the inhibition of HBV replication in HepG 2 cells harboring HBV genome.

the antisense oligodeoxynucleotides(ODN)s specific to the translations initiation sites of S(preC) and X(P) gene loci in the HBV genome inhibited the replication of HBV and HBsAg expressions, and that the treatment of the antisense ODNs to the cultured HepG2 cells inhibited the cellular DNA synthesis and cell proliferation.
we developed a new method to inhibit HBV replication in cultured cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antisense strategy is a viable option for the development of a novel therapeutic agent against hepatitis B virus infection.
the use of antisense oligonucleotides (ASO) to target HBV DNA is a viable therapeutic strategy.
the use of oligonucleotides as a potential treatment for hepatitis B virus infection is feasible.
